_comment: UHS corrections to the vendored HPG era table. HPG dates when a PEOPLE existed; several of its pools are modern name lists carrying that early floor, so a c.1900 census sample was reaching the seventeenth century. These dates are when the name FORMS IN THE POOL are attested — usually the date hereditary surnames became general, since that is what most of these pools contain. Lowering a floor here needs a reason in the note.

AFRICAN_AMERICAN.why: Pool is a c.1900 US census sample. Hereditary surnames became general after emancipation, not on arrival in 1619.

SCANDINAVIAN.why: Modern Swedish given names with frozen -sson surnames. Hereditary surname law is 19th century; 1700 is already generous. Viking-age Scandinavia needs its own tradition.

JAPANESE.why: Tanaka, Suzuki, Watanabe are koseki surnames. Commoner surnames became universal with the 1875 registration law.

THAI.why: Thai surnames date from the 1913 Surname Act; the pool carries them.

KHMER.why: Modern Khmer given names with Sino-Cambodian surnames. Angkorian onomastics are a separate, attested corpus.

MALAY.why: Modern pool; nothing in it is distinctively pre-colonial.

TURKIC_STEPPE.why: Osman, Orhan, Bayezid, Hurrem, Kosem are Seljuk-Ottoman, 13th-17th century. The pre-Mongol steppe needs Old Turkic.

SIBERIAN_INDIGENOUS.why: Given names are Sakha and Buryat; the surnames are Imperial Russian and follow the conquest.

MICRONESIAN.why: The masculine list is twentieth-century presidents and the surnames are the same men.

ZULU.why: Pool is late twentieth century. The Zulu polity itself dates from the 1810s.

SHONA.why: Given names are Christian-era sentence names.

SWAHILI_INTERIOR.why: Surnames are twentieth-century Kikuyu and Kalenjin, several of them athletes.

LEVANTINE.why: Twentieth-century Lebanese political surnames; Charbel postdates 1898.

BENGALI_TRADITIONAL.why: Masculine list is bhadralok, feminine list is film actresses.

DRAVIDIAN.why: Modern given names with caste-title surnames across four languages.

WEST_AFRICAN_SAHEL.why: Sundiata, Samori and the Mansa/Askia titles are thirteenth century and later.
